correctness.rationale: In characteristic two f′(x)=a x²+c; its sole critical root for a≠0 has a²f(r)=c²+abc+a²d=Δ, so squarefreeness is Δ≠0. Tame Kummer degree-three map has five simple full branch points including infinity giving g=3. The regular-differential Cartier matrix has C(ω0)=0, C(ω1)=ω2, C(ω2)=√cω0+√aω1; rank2 gives a-number1, stable rank zero for a=0 and two for a≠0. At a=0, L(x)=x⁴+b x²+cx is additive separable; T=ker L of order4, and involution x↦x+t has quotient z=x²+t x, E_t:z²+(c/t)z=y³+d. Nonzero c/t yields supersingular elliptic quotients. Nontrivial characters of the Klein-four translations fill H¹(C,Q_l), yielding isogeny ∏E_t→Jac(C), and Frobenius permutes summands in orbits, hence factor 1-u_O T^e+q^e T^{2e}. Counting separable cubic t³+bt+c over F_q via rational roots yields three orbit-pattern counts (q−1)(q−2)/6, q(q−1)/2, (q²−1)/3; these count coefficient models, not isomorphism classes. Independent finite-field enumerations at q=2,4,8 checked the cubic census and the original checker defines exact l-polynomial/quotient tests; the general result rests on Cartier and ℓ-adic arguments.

originality.rationale: Nart–Ritzenthaler 2003 broad char-2 nonhyperelliptic genus-3 moduli/Newton stratum is prior. Their 2009 Proposition 2.5 explicitly gives the SAME elliptic quotient equations and geometric decomposition for rationally split translations. The reviewed surviving content is an explicit coefficient-chart supersingular divisor, the three finite-field Frobenius root-splitting census, and the all-q orbit determinant factorization including nonrational involutions. These are natural descent calculations but may be implicit in general equivariant cohomology or the same authors’ broader literature; the inspected split-only primary statements do not explicitly imply the complete stated all-q census. This remains a significant priority limitation, and an inaccessible Bouw source was not declared noncovering.
